“Neubrutalism is taking over the web”

Context

Malewicz writes: “Neubrutalism, or Neobrutalism as some people call it, is a mix of regular brutalism in web design and more modern typography, illustration and animation standards.”

On shadows: “The main rule of neubrutalist shadows is to avoid using blur on them.” And: “Instead of soft shadows, it goes for hard, black rectangles under the cards. Instead of typical barely visible borders, it goes for thick, dark and defined outlines.”

He also describes pure black #000000 against color, computer-window motifs, and names Figma and Gumroad as the “two main innovators”. He notes that earlier brutalism “was mostly popular in poster-design / graphics-design”.

The GitHub Awesome Neobrutalism list places it first among articles.

Why it belongs

The best early attestation for the name. It fixes the diagnostic pair of the style (thick outline and unblurred shadow) and separates it from the raw brutalist web.
